sculpture.name: figur: djur: räv, Hårprydnad, sculpture, figure
sculpture.title: figur: djur: räv, Hårprydnad, sculpture, figure
sculpture.reason: A painted wooden carved figure/plaque with clawed arms and a crest-like head from the Maprik district, East Sepik Province — classic Abelam ceremonial carving style, consistent with the claimed culture and region.

sculpture.name: huvud, Trähuvud
sculpture.title: huvud, Trähuvud
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden painted head with elongated crest, typical of Abelam ceremonial house carvings from the Maprik/Wosera region, East Sepik Province, matching the claimed ethnicity and findspot exactly.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden standing male figure with a bird-crowned headdress, polychrome painted with the red, yellow, black and white pigment designs characteristic of Abelam ancestor/ceremonial figures from Papua New Guinea's East Sepik region. This is a classic example of Abelam sculptural tradition.

sculpture.name: Trähuvud, huvud
sculpture.title: Trähuvud, huvud
sculpture.reason: A small carved wooden head, flat-backed and painted in beige, brown and red, collected in the Wosera area of the Maprik district (East Sepik), the heartland of Abelam carving — consistent with Abelam ancestral/ritual carving traditions.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden standing human figure attributed to the Abelam people of Papua New Guinea, consistent with their ancestor/spirit figure carving tradition.

household.name: kam
household.title: kam
household.reason: The object is a "kam" (comb) made of five pointed wood sticks bound with plaited fiber and decorated with feathers, collected from the Abelam people at Niamingum, Maprik district, East Sepik Province — a typical Abelam-made personal/grooming implement.

household.name: Träpall, pall
household.title: Träpall, pall
household.reason: A carved wooden stool with five curved legs, collected at Maundu in the Maprik district of East Sepik province, the heartland of the Abelam people; such wooden stools are typical household/ritual furniture in this region.

household.name: väska, nätväska, bag, bolsa
household.title: väska, nätväska, bag, bolsa
household.reason: A netted string bag (bilum-type) from the Wosera area of Maprik district, East Sepik Province — the Abelam heartland — matching plant-fiber construction with brown-dyed pattern bands typical of the region.

household.name: klämma, Träklämma
household.title: klämma, Träklämma
household.reason: A wooden clamp carved in one piece with a bird-form top, used for securing sago filter straps, collected in Maundu, Maprik district (Abelam homeland) in 1955-56. This is a plausible traditional Abelam household/utility tool.

household.name: nätväska, väska, bag, bolsa
household.title: nätväska, väska, bag, bolsa
household.reason: A fiber net bag (bilum-type) with banded polychrome patterning, collected in Wosera, Maprik district, East Sepik Province — the Abelam heartland — used as a carrying bag with strap doubling as a headband, consistent with Abelam material culture.

arms.name: dagger; knife
arms.title: dagger; knife
arms.reason: A bone dagger with incised ornament, attributed by the museum directly to the Abelam; bone daggers (often made from cassowary leg bone) are a well-known Abelam/Sepik weapon type.

arms.name: dolk, kniv, knife
arms.title: dolk, kniv, knife
arms.reason: A cassowary-bone dagger with carved low-relief ornament, collected in the Wosera area of the Maprik district (Abelam heartland in East Sepik), consistent with known Abelam dagger production.

arms.name: yxa, Tväryxblad
arms.title: yxa, Tväryxblad
arms.reason: A ground stone axe/adze blade, with findspot in the Maprik district of East Sepik Province attributed to Abelam territory (possibly Malmba or Maundu villages) — a tool/weapon type used by this people.

arms.name: dagger; knife
arms.title: dagger; knife
arms.reason: A bone dagger with incised ornament, a well-known Abelam/Sepik region weapon type typically made from cassowary bone with a carved end-knob; museum attributes it to the Abelam.

arms.name: dagger; knife
arms.title: dagger; knife
arms.reason: A bone dagger (likely made from cassowary leg bone) with carved ornament at the handle, a well-documented traditional weapon type of the Abelam and neighboring Sepik peoples of Papua New Guinea.

ceramic.name: kärl, skål, vessel
ceramic.title: kärl, skål, vessel
ceramic.reason: A small coconut-shell vessel with incised low-relief spiral and curvilinear decoration, collected in the Maprik district of East Sepik Province, the Abelam heartland, matching known Abelam carved coconut-shell containers.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: This is a classic Abelam yam mask (baba/kabaak-style) made of rattan framework, grass, hair and chalk with red/black pigment, used to decorate long yams at harvest ceremonies — a well-documented Abelam ritual art form matching the museum's own attribution.

masks-ritual.name: ornament; dance equipment
masks-ritual.title: ornament; dance equipment
masks-ritual.reason: The image shows a karawut, a plaited fibre ritual ornament decorated with nassa shells and boar's tusks, worn or carried in dance by the Abelam of Papua New Guinea — a classic ritual/masking adornment consistent with the claimed culture.

masks-ritual.name: mask; ceremonial equipment
masks-ritual.title: mask; ceremonial equipment
masks-ritual.reason: A basketry fiber mask with painted red/brown/yellow/white eye panels and wood toggle fastening, consistent with Abelam yam ceremony masks worn over yam tubers during harvest display. This matches the claimed culture and recorded purpose well.

masks-ritual.name: mask; ceremonial equipment
masks-ritual.title: mask; ceremonial equipment
masks-ritual.reason: Basketry yam-ceremony mask with openwork teeth and ochre/yellow/red/white coloring, attributed by the museum to the Abelam, who are well known for elaborate yam-cult basketry masks worn on long yams during harvest festivals. Fits both ethnicity and ritual use.

masks-ritual.name: mask, Ansiktsmask
masks-ritual.title: mask, Ansiktsmask
masks-ritual.reason: A spirally woven rattan/cane face mask with concentric oval coils, painted in red, brown and grayish-white, from Maprik district, East Sepik Province — the Abelam heartland; this coiled cane mask type is characteristic of Abelam yam-cult ceremonies.

masks-ritual.name: mask; religious/ritual equipment
masks-ritual.title: mask; religious/ritual equipment
masks-ritual.reason: This is a classic Abelam yam cult mask made of plaited vegetable fibre with long chain-like fibre appendages and traces of red pigment, consistent with Abelam ceremonial yam/initiation regalia from the East Sepik region.

jewelry.name: hårprydnad
jewelry.title: hårprydnad
jewelry.reason: A slim wooden hair ornament with feathers stuck into it, collected in the Maprik district (Abelam heartland) of East Sepik Province, consistent with Abelam hair decoration worn in ceremonial dress.

jewelry.name: halsband, necklace
jewelry.title: halsband, necklace
jewelry.reason: A long cowrie-shell necklace collected in Malmba, Maprik district, East Sepik Province — the Abelam heartland — a typical traditional ornament worn there.

instruments.name: flöjt, flute
instruments.title: flöjt, flute
instruments.reason: A coconut-shell vessel flute with two holes and incised zigzag decoration, collected in Maundu, Maprik district, East Sepik — the Abelam heartland — matching a traditional musical instrument of this people.
